a: Contract tests verify producer/consumer API agreements without full end-to-end stacks.
Property-based tests check invariants across many generated inputs.
Mutation testing changes code slightly to see if tests catch the mutants.
Snapshot tests compare UI/output against a stored baseline.
Many unit tests, fewer integration tests, fewest expensive e2e tests.
Test doubles include mocks, stubs, fakes, and spies.
AAA pattern: arrange data, act on system, assert results.
Flakes often come from time, order dependence, shared state, or network.
Parallelize independent tests to cut CI wall-clock time.
High coverage does not guarantee quality; still need meaningful assertions.
Chaos tests inject failures (latency, kill nodes) to verify resilience.
Visual regression testing detects unintended UI pixel/layout changes.
